introduces.whales: Cloud whales sweep their long fins through the mist above a grassy island.

introduces.olivia: Lady Olivia, the unicorn Riftseeker you met on the glacier, waits with a notebook.

introduces.whale_approach: The keeper unfolds a cloth map.

introduces.whale_notch: A smaller whale with a notched fin vanishes into moving banks of mist.

introduces.whale_greeting: The keeper can teach a quiet note or a slow arm signal.

introduces.whale_cloth: a rolled shelter cloth starts sliding past her hoof

introduces.whale_small_turn: A little whale turns toward the open lane

introduces.whale_new_keeper: A new kitsune keeper arrives to take over

introduces.whale_report: It is a promise to bring news, not to make the whales return.

introduces.valley_arrival: Pip Thistledown, a young manticore scout, stops so suddenly that his notebook bumps his nose.

introduces.look_again: An old route marker has a fork-shaped chip.

introduces.valley_worksite: A yeti route worker meets you on the near bank.

introduces.valley_routes: The calm pocket leads to a low shelf crossing.

introduces.valley_priority: There is time for one preparation before your party crosses.

introduces.valley_signals: The workers demonstrate their crossing signs:

introduces.valley_crossing: The low shelf has a guide rope and a calm pocket.

introduces.valley_return: Water noses into the old bed while the western stream grows quieter.

introduces.valley_change: The river runs in its older bed again.

introduces.valley_record: both river lines and the order of the change recorded

introduces.room_arrival: An elder yeti welcomes you into a room cut from the glacier.

introduces.quiet_rule: The elder sets a cup of tea beside the marked floor.

introduces.witness_first: The route worker gives the elder a drawing of the two valleys.

introduces.catalog_cards: The elder lays out three cards for the same memory.

introduces.listening_floor: A faint low song travels through the floor from a hall elsewhere in the ice.

introduces.support_ice: The close reading place needs a settled cradle to catch flakes.

introduces.second_view: The elder leads you to a second marked viewpoint, still on the safe floor.

introduces.what_matches: The outside drawing and memory account lie on the elder's table.

introduces.catalog_test: A younger yeti keeper brings a fresh catalog slip.

introduces.sliding_tray: A shallow tray holds blank slips and chalk.

introduces.compare_accounts: The elder asks whether your party has another checked observation of a river where today's geography does not fit it.

introduces.record_choice: The elder offers to keep a copy of your party's finished comparison.

introduces.teach_back: An arriving yeti visitor waits at the warm cup.

introduces.island_arrival: a folded landing board, signal cloths and a wooden box of song slips

introduces.island_song: The keeper opens the song box.

introduces.island_sightings: A notch on the approaching island slides past a distant cloud break.

introduces.island_priority: A gust rattles the song box.

introduces.island_letters: The mailbag catches inside the fence.

introduces.island_station: The signal frame rocks in the wet grass.

introduces.island_signals: The keeper lays out the cloths: white means watch; striped means stop.

introduces.island_window: The returning island clears the cloud with its flat shelf and stone's empty eye.

introduces.island_landing: The keeper lays the board between the close shelves.

introduces.island_stone: On the returning island, a round hole looks through an old standing stone.

introduces.island_copy: The shallow grooves are hard to separate from grass shadows.

introduces.island_orientation: Three ridges show through the cloud below.

introduces.island_comparison: Three raised marks appear on your copy beside today's three-ridge sketch.

introduces.island_limits: Pip looks from the stone to the lookout sketch.

introduces.island_permission: The keeper asks permission to keep a copy of your observations.

introduces.island_handoff: The temple roofs appear through the cloud ahead.

introduces.island_recovery_kit: The keeper has a checked crossing, but your bulky kit is awkward in this wind.

introduces.skupper_guide: On the Saltrot mudflats, an opening in the air blinks away and comes back. Through it lies snow. A snowhorn goat stands belly-deep in mud beside it, chewing a reed with great disappointment. Your Skupper guide from the Saltrot bank waves her fins in greeting, then points to the rising tide. "Bring that goat home before the opening closes. I can find firm mud. I cannot make a goat like it."
introduces.blinking_gap: an opening in the air blinks

introduces.yard_guide: At the edge of the Bone Yard, your Skupper guide from the flats stops in a brackish pool. Beyond her, broken stone walls have appeared among enormous old bones. Small bone crawlers crowd the fresh shimmer around the walls. "Clear a safe way past those ruins," she says. "Take nothing. Here, anything taken comes back. I will watch from water that suits my fins." One crawler is trying to fit its whole body under a pebble.

introduces.nest_bench: using a bench as a pillow

introduces.temple_keeper: The island you helped welcome home is drifting toward a temple island through heavy rain. A different kitsune keeper from the one at the lookout rings a lookout bell; its rope wears a tiny raincoat. Beside the temple, a fresh opening spills bone crawlers onto the wet landing: little scuttling creatures with jointed legs and rattling backs. "Keep the temple safe as that island drifts toward us," the keeper calls. "We can push its approach clear, or shelter this landing and let it settle." She points to people still carrying cushions across the yard.

introduces.converge_travelers: At a sheltered glacier ledge, Orin waves you over to a map on an upturned sled. Olivia greets you and steadies one corner. Your Riftseeker friends have made room for your account. A bigfoot named Bram Lock keeps the path clear. "Help me keep everyone behind the line when an opening comes," he asks. Orin weights the map with his boot. "Compare your discoveries. Then help us steady any opening before people go near it." His boot is still on his foot.
